d:
Delhi's air pollution crisis is raising serious public health concerns, with three major hospitals reporting 6,581 lung cancer cases and four hospitals recording 913 lung cancer deaths. As Delhi battles toxic air and dangerous PM2.5 levels, the long-term health consequences of prolonged exposure to air pollution are coming into sharper focus.
On November 26, Delhi's PM2.5 concentration stood at 148.1 g/m³ at 6:30 AM before dropping to 127 g/m³ at 9:30 AM. These readings have been compared to the equivalent of 6.7 and 5.8 cigarettes a day respectively.
